 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.12,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 22.2.2018 at about 8.45 p.m. the petitioner was a pillion rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-11-EF-3815.

The rider was proceeding on Hosahalli road, Dodda Gollarahatti, Bengaluru at that time, the rider of the said vehicle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and jumped the path holes and apply the sudden break.

As a result of the forced impact,
the petitioner was thrown out fell down and sustained grievous injuries on the vital parts of the body.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Srikrishna Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein after first aid treatment was offered and admitted as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 24 years, electrician and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor bike bearing No.KA-11-EF-3815.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and the respondent No.1 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement.
5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further this respondent has denied about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No. ka-11-ef- 3815 and its validity.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S.
158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
Further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.
6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor Shri Sachin B.G vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company on 15 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7056894/
2 cycle bearing No.KA-11-EF-3815 on 2.2.2018 at about 8.45 p.m. on Hosahalli Road,
Dododa Gollarhatti, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10, and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P11 to Ex.P13.
8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:-
During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that, to prove the disablement, the petitioner has examined Dr.Aruju S.Pakash as PW2, who has assessed 46.8% of left upper limb and 15.6% of whole body disability.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.1.
13. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of his evidence, he has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P5 such as FIR with complaint,
Spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
15. On perusal of Ex.
P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by Gangaraju, Son of Late Chickputtaiah on 23.2.2018.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Byadarahalli Police in Cr. No.152/2018 against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-11-EF-3815 for the Shri Sachin B.G vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company on 15 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7056894/
3 offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.

sentences.text: Ex . P3
is the IMV report reveals that the damages caused to both the vehicles and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex.P4 is the spot mahazar also reveals the scene of occurrence and it corroborate the evidence of PW1.
On perusal of Ex.P4 wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P5 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the car for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
16.
The counsel for the respondent No.1 has denied the manner of the accident.
But, to substantiate the said fact, the respondent No.1 has not led any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner.
On the other hand petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 18. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that he met with an accident on 22.2.2018 at about 8.45 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Krishna Hospital,
Benglauru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P4, which discloses the following injuries;
1) Shoulder dislocation right 2) Labral tear right 20.
The doctor is of the opinion that the injury Nos. 1 and 2 are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 22.2.2018 to 24.2.2018.
The petitioner has also produced another discharge summary, which discloses that the petitioner took the treatment as inpatient from 26.3.2018 to 31.3.2018.
21. PW2- Dr.Arjun S.Prakash has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained above said injuries.

He has produced inpatient record, x-ray and MRI, which are marked at Ex.P11 to Ex.P13.
22.

Considering the oral evidence of PW1 & PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 24 years, Electrician and getting an income of Rs.18,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any documents pertains to his avocation and income.
In the absence of the documents pertains to his avocation and income, it is very difficult to assess the income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner, if notional income of Rs.8,500/- per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 22.2.2018 to 24.2.2018.
The petitioner has also produced another discharge summary, which discloses that the petitioner took the treatment as inpatient from 26.3.2018 to 31.3.2018.

The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries;
he might have taken rest and treatment at least for two months.
Therefore, two months income comes to Rs.17,000/- is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
24. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
On record he has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P8 to the extent of Rs.1,26,065/- supported with prescriptions at Ex.P9,
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,26,025/- towards medical expenses.
25. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 24 years, working as a Electrician and getting an income of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he cannot sit, squat, walk for long distance, cannot weight, cannot walk without support.
26. To prove the age, the petitioner has produced Aadhar card marked at Ex.P10.
On perusal of the same the date of birth of the petitioner was mentioned as 2.3.1993.
The accident occurred on 22.2.2018.
So, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 24 years.
So, same is considered as the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident 27.
PW2-Dr.Arjun S.Prakash has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and assessed the permanent disability.
According to him, the petitioner has 46.8% of upper lower limb and 15.6% of whole body disability.

So, considering the evidence of PW2 and the cross-examination and the age and avocation of the petitioner and relative disability, if 12% is considered as whole body of disability of the petitioner, it will meet the ends of justice.
The petitioner age is already considered as 24 years the multiplier applicable to this age is 18.
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.2,20,320/- under the head of loss of future earning.
29. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained fractures.
So his happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out his life.
Hence, it is just and necessary to award compensation of Rs.5,000/- under the head of amenities.

5 30.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident he took the treatment as inpatient from 22.2.2018 to 24.2.2018.
The petitioner has also produced another discharge summary, which discloses that the petitioner took the treatment as inpatient from 26.3.2018 to 31.3.2018..
He took the treatment as inpatient and also took the treatment as outpatient.
So, one must attend him during the above said period.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.
31.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:

during laid period Rs. 17,000-00 and rest period
3. Medical expenses Rs. 1,26,025-00 4. Loss of future income Rs. 2,20,320-00 5. Loss of amenities, Rs. 5,000-00
6. Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 15,000-00.
conveyance charges
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-11-EF-3815.
33.
The respondent No.1 has denied about the issuance of the policy in respect of motor cycle bearing No.KA-11-EF-3815 and its validity.
On perusal of cause title of the claim petition the policy is valid from 30.8.2017 to 29.8.2018.
The accident occurred on 22.2.2018.
So, as o the date of accident the policy was in existence, same has not been challenged by the respondent.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
34. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;

6 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,23,345/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any nationalized/scheduled bank for a period of three years and remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 15th day of April 2019).
